findings.title: Unhealthy flusher process is never killed before being restarted
findings.body: `_ensure_processes_alive` now guards the kill with `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. The processes are created via `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`, i.e. `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess`, which derives from `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess` and is *not* a subclass of `multiprocessing.Process` (`multiprocessing.context.Process`). The isinstance check is therefore always False, so `process.kill()` is never executed — the previous code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally. Consequence: when a flusher is detected as hung (`cause == "hang"`, process still alive but `healthy_since` stale), the old process keeps running while `_create_process_for_shards` spawns a second process for the same shards. Two processes then flush the same Redis shards concurrently, which can produce duplicate/partial segments to the buffered-segments topic, and up to MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS+1 processes can accumulate per shard group. Use `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess` (or check for `threading.Thread` instead) in the guard.

findings.title: join() skips termination of remaining processes once the deadline expires
findings.body: In `join`, the loop over `self.processes.items()` does `if remaining_time <= 0: break` before waiting on each process. If the first process consumes the whole timeout budget, every remaining process is skipped entirely — it is neither waited for nor terminated. Combined with the `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` check at the end of the loop (always False for spawn-context `SpawnProcess`, see the kill() issue), `terminate()` is effectively never called on any flusher process, so hung flusher processes can outlive the shutdown/rebalance path. `remaining_time` is also computed and then unused except for the comparison. Consider terminating all processes after the wait loop regardless of which ones timed out, and fixing the isinstance check.

findings.title: Per-segment metric now tagged with a high-cardinality shard-list tag
findings.body: `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` is emitted for every flushed segment and is now tagged with `shard=shard_tag`, where `shard_tag` is the comma-joined list of all shards handled by that process (e.g. `"0,3,6,9"` or, with the default `--flusher-processes 1`, the full assigned-partition list). That tag value changes on every Kafka rebalance and differs per consumer instance, so this high-volume metric gains an effectively unbounded set of tag values. The same tag is added to the `spans.buffer.flusher.produce`/`wait_produce` timers and to `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy`. This risks cardinality blowup/cost in the metrics backend; consider emitting a per-shard tag only where the value is a single bounded shard id, or dropping the tag from the per-segment metric.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag key: "shards" vs "shard"
findings.body: `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` is tagged with `{"shards": shard_tag}` while `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` use `{"shard": shard_tag}` for the same value. Dashboards/alerts grouping by `shard` will silently miss the `wait_produce` timer. Pick one key.

findings.title: Class docstring claims one process per shard, which is not what the code does
findings.body: The docstring says "Creates one process per shard for parallel processing." In practice the number of processes is `min(max_processes, len(assigned_shards))` and shards are round-robined onto processes, and the CLI default for `--flusher-processes` is 1, so the default behaviour is a single process handling all shards. The new `max_processes` parameter is also undocumented while the docstring still documents a non-existent `topic` parameter. This misleads operators about the default behaviour.

findings.title: Dead method _create_process_for_shard
findings.body: `_create_process_for_shard(shard)` is not called anywhere after the refactor (`_ensure_processes_alive` calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` directly). It duplicates restart logic and will silently drift out of sync; remove it or wire it up.

findings.title: --flusher-processes 0 silently means "one process per shard"
findings.body: `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats 0 as falsy, so passing `--flusher-processes 0` (or any code path passing 0) results in one process per assigned shard rather than an error or a single process. The click option has no range validation. Use an explicit `if max_processes is None` and/or validate `>= 1` in the click option.

findings.title: Redis memory info is now queried once per flusher buffer on every submit
findings.body: `submit` previously called `self.buffer.get_memory_info()` once; it now iterates `self.buffers.values()` and calls `get_memory_info()` on each of the N per-process buffers (plus `record_stored_segments()` on each). Since each `SpansBuffer` holds its own client, these calls duplicate the Redis INFO round trips N times per submitted message batch when `spans.buffer.max-memory-percentage < 1.0`, scaling with `--flusher-processes`. If a given Redis node is reported by more than one buffer, both `used` and `available` are also counted multiple times. Consider keeping a single buffer in the parent for memory/stat reporting.

findings.title: Added time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched
findings.body: Line 15 does `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`, so the newly added `time.sleep(0.1)` on line 62 ("Give flusher threads time to process after drift change") does nothing at all. The comment is misleading and the test still relies entirely on `step.join()` busy-looping for the flusher thread to produce the message, so it remains timing-dependent. Either drop the sleep/comment or use an unpatched sleep (e.g. capture the original `time.sleep` before monkeypatching) / poll until `messages` is non-empty.

findings.title: New multiprocess flusher test only asserts bookkeeping, not behaviour
findings.body: `test_flusher_processes_limit` submits no messages and only asserts `len(flusher.processes) == 2`, `max_processes`, `num_processes` and that the shard map totals 4. It does not assert that shards are partitioned without overlap (e.g. `{0,1,2,3}` exactly once across `process_to_shards_map`), nor that segments from all 4 shards are actually flushed/produced when more than one process is used. The core risk of this PR — multiple flushers each owning a disjoint shard subset and producing all segments exactly once — is untested. There is also no test for the unhealthy-process restart path that this PR rewrote.
